skill.name: hig-components-layout
skill.description: Apple Human Interface Guidelines guidance for layout and navigation components across Apple platforms. It helps choose sidebars, split views, tab bars, tab views, scroll views, windows, panels, lists, tables, boxes, and ornaments.
skill.summary: Choose Apple HIG layout and navigation patterns for adaptive app interfaces.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Apple app layouts can break when navigation patterns do not match platform expectations. This skill applies Apple HIG guidance to choose adaptive layout and navigation components.
actual_capabilities: Recommends navigation patterns for sidebars, tab bars, split views, tab views, and column views.
Maps layouts across iPhone, iPad, Mac, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS constraints.
Summarizes HIG guidance for lists, tables, outline views, windows, panels, boxes, and ornaments.
Provides adaptation checklists for size classes, multitasking, orientation, and accessibility.
Identifies when a layout should use system components instead of custom navigation.
limitations: It provides design guidance, not a complete implementation.
It does not replace testing on real devices and window sizes.
It depends on included reference notes, which may lag future Apple updates.
It cannot evaluate visuals unless you provide screenshots or design details.

use_cases.title: Choose an App Navigation Pattern
use_cases.description: Decide whether an Apple app should use tabs, a sidebar, split views, or stacked navigation.

use_cases.title: Review Adaptive Layout Behavior
use_cases.description: Check how a layout should change across compact width, regular width, multitasking, and windowed states.

use_cases.title: Standardize Component Guidance
use_cases.description: Create consistent rules for lists, tables, panels, windows, ornaments, and grouped content.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Navigation
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building an Apple app with [sections] for [platforms]. Recommend a navigation pattern and explain the hierarchy.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt Existing Layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this layout plan for [app type]. Explain how it should adapt on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and visionOS.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare tab bars, sidebars, split views, and tab views for this information architecture: [details]. Include tradeoffs and platform risks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Navigation Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Apple app navigation model against HIG layout guidance. Identify mismatches, missing states, and safer component choices.

output_examples.input: A notes app has folders, note lists, note details, and an optional inspector on iPad and Mac.
output_examples.output: Recommended pattern: sidebar with split detail. Use a folder sidebar, a note list pane, a detail pane, and an optional inspector.

output_examples.input: A fitness app has five peer sections and shallow content on iPhone and iPad.
output_examples.output: Recommended pattern: tab bar first. Keep the tab labels short, preserve each tab state, and consider sidebar adaptation on iPad.

output_examples.input: A visionOS media app needs playback tools without covering the main window content.
output_examples.output: Recommended pattern: use an ornament for frequent controls. Keep it balanced, close to the window, and narrower than the content.

best_practices: Provide the app structure, target platforms, and top-level section count before asking for a recommendation.
Ask for separate behavior across compact, regular, multitasking, and windowed states.
Use the output as a design checklist and verify it with real-device testing.
anti_patterns: Requesting a single layout without platform or content hierarchy details.
Using a sidebar on every screen when a tab bar or list is simpler.
Treating HIG guidance as implementation code without checking framework behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill write SwiftUI code?
faq.answer: It can suggest component choices and structure, but it is primarily design guidance.

faq.question: Which Apple platforms does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS where the included references apply.

faq.question: Can it choose between tabs and sidebars?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares the information architecture, platform, screen size, and number of top-level sections.

faq.question: Can it help with iPad resizing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for split view behavior, sidebars, window resizing, and multitasking states.

faq.question: Does it use live Apple documentation?
faq.answer: No. It uses the reference files included in the skill package.

faq.question: Can it review screenshots?
faq.answer: It can use screenshots if the host AI tool supports image input, but the skill itself provides text guidance.
